study_type_evidence.quote: In two separate experiments, S-20-1 was administered either OP or IP to C57BL/6 mice at the dose of 50 mg/kg, volume 150 µL.
we employed PAMPA-BBB to evaluate the ability of S-20-1 to penetrate the BBB and PAMPA-GIT to determine the gastrointestinal absorption rate

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: C57BL/6 (pharmacokinetic study); sex and age not reported
in_vivo_species.quote: S-20-1 was administered either OP or IP to C57BL/6 mice at the dose of 50 mg/kg

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: newborn Balb/c pups from pregnant dams (HCoV-OC43 challenge model); seven newborn mice per group
in_vivo_species.quote: Pregnant Balb/c mice (18 days) were separated into three groups after delivery of their offspring. Each group contained seven newborn mice.
in_vivo_species.section: METHODS (Evaluation of the in vivo protective activity of S-20-1)

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: C57BL/6-Tgtn (CAG-human ACE2-IRES-Luciferase-WPRE-polyA) hACE2-transgenic, female, 8 weeks old
in_vivo_species.quote: Eight-week-old female hACE2 transgenic mice were challenged with SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant at 10,000 pfu via the intranasal route.
in_vivo_species.section: METHODS (Evaluation of the in vivo protective activity of S-20-1)

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: Balb/c, eight weeks old (in vivo safety study); sex not reported
in_vivo_species.quote: Eight-week-old Balb/c mice were used to test the in vivo safety of S-20-1.
in_vivo_species.section: RESULTS (S-20-1 had good in vivo safety profiles in mouse model)

in_vitro_detail: Cell-cell fusion assays in 293T effector / Huh-7 target cells; pseudovirus and authentic virus infection assays in Huh-7, Caco-2 and RD cells; cytotoxicity (CCK-8); FITC-uptake imaging in HeLa cells; fluorescence-polarization binding to S1, RBD, HR1, HR2; PAMPA-BBB and PAMPA-GIT artificial-membrane permeability; proteolytic stability with purified proteinase K, trypsin and Pronase followed by RP-HPLC.

agents.name: S-20-1
agents.sequence_source: Cyclic γ-AApeptide peptidomimetic built from unnatural AApeptide building blocks; only a chemical structure drawing is given (Fig. 2a), no one-letter amino-acid sequence is printed in the body.
agents.chemical_identifier: S-20-1, a modified thioether-bridged cyclic γ-AApeptide derived from hit S-20 by addition of two negative charges; structure shown in Fig. 2a
agents.group_n: n = 3 per time point (9 mice per route, 18 mice total) for PK; 7 newborn mice per group for HCoV-OC43 efficacy; n = 6 per group for safety
agents.group_n_quote: n = 3 per time point, and each mouse was used for three time points; thus 9 mice were used for either OP or IP
agents.dose: 50 mg/kg (PK, single dose); 80 mg/kg intranasal (HCoV-OC43 efficacy); 60 mg/kg intranasal (SARS-CoV-2 Delta efficacy); 100 mg/kg intranasal daily x3 (safety)
agents.route: intraperitoneal and oral (PK); intranasal (efficacy and safety)
agents.dose_route_quote: S-20-1 was administered either OP or IP to C57BL/6 mice at the dose of 50 mg/kg, volume 150 µL.
agents.cmax: 120,637 µg/L (intraperitoneal); oral Cmax not reported in body text
agents.pk_quote: For IP administration, S-20-1 demonstrated excellent PK parameters with a long half-life (T1/2) of 14.53 h and a high peak concentration (Cmax) of 120,637 µg/L
agents.pk_section: RESULTS (S-20-1 exhibited excellent pharmacokinetic (PK) profile and oral bioavailability tested in mouse model)

agents.name: S-20
agents.sequence_source: Parent cyclic γ-AApeptide hit; chemical structure drawn in Fig. 1c and Fig. 7a, no amino-acid sequence printed.
agents.chemical_identifier: S-20, unmodified cyclic γ-AApeptide hit from the OBTC library
agents.dose: 100 μM in PAMPA-BBB assay; 1 μM in cell-uptake imaging; not administered in vivo
agents.dose_route_quote: S-20 and S-20-1 at 100 μM displayed favorable permeability with Papp values of 536 × 10−6 cm/s and 30 × 10−6 cm/s, respectively

agents.name: PBS
agents.group_n_quote: Eight-week-old mice (two groups, n = 6) were used to evaluate the safety of S-20-1 in vivo.
agents.dose_route_quote: Body weight changes of mice administered with S-20-1 or PBS intranasally.

agents.name: Verapamil
agents.chemical_identifier: not reported (no CAS or catalogue number in body)
agents.dose_route_quote: Verapamil (positive control) at 50 μM and Theophylline (negative control) at 250 μM exhibited Papp values of 155 × 10−6 and <10 × 10−6 cm/s

agents.name: Theophylline
agents.dose_route_quote: For the PAMPA-BBB assay, we used Verapamil as positive control and Theophylline as negative control.

agents.name: Carbamazepine
agents.dose: not reported (concentration not stated for GIT assay)
agents.dose_route_quote: Carbamazepine is fully orally bioavailable with favorable permeability at pH 5.0, 6.2, and 7.4

agents.name: Antipyrine
agents.dose_route_quote: Antipyrine is poorly orally bioavailable with low Papp values at different pH values

concentration_time_figure.locator: Fig. 8c (with parameter table in Fig. 8d and Supplementary Fig. S10)
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Time-concentration plot of S-20-1 in PK study. Plasma concentration and time curve following intraperitoneal (IP) (red) and oral administration (OP) (blue) administration of 50 mg/kg S-20-1 in C57BL/6 mice
concentration_time_figure.note: Plasma concentration versus time over 48 h after a single 50 mg/kg dose by both IP and oral routes; means ± SD, n = 3.

bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS on protein-precipitated (acetonitrile/glacial acetic acid) mouse plasma; PK parameters computed with PKSolver
bioanalytical_quote: Clarified supernatants were transferred to vials and analyzed by LC/MS/MS. PK parameters were obtained using PKSolver.
notes: S-20-1 is a cyclic γ-AApeptide peptidomimetic, not a natural peptide; no amino-acid sequence or SMILES is printed in the body, only chemical structure drawings (Figs. 1c, 2a, 7a). PK reported only for S-20-1 (50 mg/kg IP and oral in C57BL/6 mice): T1/2 14.53 h IP and 24.29 h oral, Cmax 120,637 µg/L IP, oral bioavailability ~2.4%. Tmax, AUC and oral Cmax are not given in the body text (referred to Fig. 8d/Supplementary Fig. S10 tables not reproduced in the text). Proteolytic-stability experiments used purified proteinase K, trypsin and Pronase rather than serum or plasma, so they are classified in vitro and no ex vivo arm is recorded. The header of the source file lists 'PMID: ?'; the assigned PMID 36075899 was used.
